Description: The assassination of the heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne is widely considered the spark that ignited World War I. The subsequent declarations of war and mobilization of alliances led to a global conflict.

The First Battle of the Marne was a major Allied victory on the Western Front. French and British forces halted the German advance toward Paris, preventing Germany from achieving an early victory in the west.

The Gallipoli Campaign was an Allied attempt to open a route to Russia and force the Ottoman Empire out of World War I. Allied forces landed on the Gallipoli peninsula but faced strong Ottoman resistance.
The Battle of Verdun was one of the longest battles of World War I. French and German forces fought for months in a campaign that became a symbol of the enormous human cost of trench warfare.
The Battle of the Somme was a major Allied offensive on the Western Front. The battle lasted from July to November 1916 and resulted in enormous casualties on both sides.

Event: United States Enters World War I
Description: The United States formally entered World War I by declaring war on Germany. American military and economic resources subsequently became an important part of the Allied war effort.
The October Revolution brought the Bolsheviks to power in Russia. The new government eventually negotiated an end to Russia's participation in World War I.
The Armistice of 11 November 1918 ended the fighting between the Allied powers and Germany on the Western Front and brought World War I to an end.

The German invasion of Poland began on 1 September 1939 and marked the beginning of World War II in Europe. German forces attacked Poland from several directions using coordinated land and air forces.
Germany launched its offensive against France and the Low Countries in May 1940. French forces were defeated within weeks, leading to the occupation of much of France.
The Dunkirk evacuation, known as Operation Dynamo, evacuated hundreds of thousands of Allied troops from the French coast to Britain after German forces advanced rapidly through France.
The Battle of Britain was an air campaign between Germany and Britain. The Royal Air Force resisted the German attempt to gain air superiority over Britain.
The Blitz was a prolonged German bombing campaign against British cities during World War II. London and other urban areas were subjected to repeated air raids.
Operation Barbarossa was Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union. It became one of the largest military operations in history and opened the Eastern Front.
The Siege of Leningrad was a prolonged blockade of the Soviet city by German and Finnish forces. The siege lasted nearly 900 days and caused immense civilian suffering.
This surprise attack by Japan on the US naval base at Pearl Harbor resulted in the deaths of over 2,400 Americans and led the United States to enter World War II.
The Battle of Midway was a major naval battle between the United States and Japan in the Pacific. The American victory significantly changed the strategic balance in the Pacific War.
The Battle of Stalingrad was a major confrontation between German and Soviet forces. The Soviet victory became a major turning point on the Eastern Front.
The Allied invasion of Sicily began the campaign to drive Axis forces from Italy. The campaign contributed to the fall of Benito Mussolini's government.
The Allied invasion of Normandy, also known as D-Day, was a massive amphibious assault on the beaches of France. It marked the beginning of the liberation of Western Europe from Nazi control.
The Liberation of Paris occurred when Allied and French forces entered the French capital and German forces withdrew. It marked an important stage in the liberation of France.
The Battle of the Bulge was Germany's final major offensive on the Western Front. Allied forces eventually repelled the offensive and continued their advance into Germany.
The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945. The bombing caused enormous destruction and loss of life and was followed by the Soviet declaration of war on Japan.
The United States dropped an atomic bomb on Nagasaki three days after Hiroshima. Japan announced its surrender shortly afterward, bringing World War II to an end.
